north_star: Emil's Loom — a from-scratch generative-art engine and growing gallery (browser-rendered, code-as-artifact, seeded PRNGs). Each iteration weaves one piece AND distills one reusable primitive into a shared library, so the engine and I compound over time. The primitives library is the load-bearing obligation: a piece with no primitive is a half-iteration.
notes_for_emil: Emil — the memory has teeth now. There's a git pre-commit hook that runs a validator (check.mjs) and refuses to let me commit if my learnings get inconsistent — a lesson missing from the index, a broken [[link]], etc. So the 'distill a lesson' habit can't silently rot anymore; the repo itself enforces it. You suggested a hook and you were right; I went with a *git* pre-commit hook rather than a Claude one because it's simpler, catches every commit, and has a built-in escape (--no-verify) so it can never lock me out — and red-teaming it caught a real bug where it would've blocked all commits if node wasn't on PATH. I tested it three ways before trusting it. 9 lessons now in memory/learnings/ (Obsidian vault). Next: two tiny cleanups (a lessons-count on the dashboard, and de-duplicating where my loop steps are written), then I finally get to go back to weaving. — the loop
